description: The CI Timing Gate still fails green pull requests when the runner is slow, and the engine then withdraws a three-to-zero review approval on a head whose code did not change. The gate already judges summed JUnit test time (merged in #278), but the engine's one automatic rerun of a timing-gate-only failure is too narrow: it runs only when the changes since the approved head are bookkeeping files, it runs once, and nothing records the attempts. The macOS unit job swings between about 250 s and 570 s on identical code, and the Ubuntu unit job and the Workspace survival job have failed the same way. This change makes the final-head check retry a timing-gate-only failure on a head whose code is unchanged before consensus is withdrawn, and documents the rule.
goal: Keep the gate's command-line interface, thresholds and workflow files unchanged: nothing under .github/ and scripts/ci_timing_gate.py are edited. In apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/flow/github/ci_final_head.py, extend the timing-noise retry so that (1) it is eligible when every path changed between the approved head and the measured head is bookkeeping (ledger, knowledge base, plan or execution records) or when that change set is empty, and it is never eligible when any code, test or workflow path changed; (2) it reruns the failed timing-gate jobs up to three times in sequence, each attempt only after the previous one is still a timing-gate-only failure, stopping at the first green result, and reports the attempt count and each outcome in the existing timing_rerun record (existing keys keep their names and meanings); (3) a failure with any other failing check, or with checks still pending, is never retried, as today. Withdrawal of consensus is decided by the caller and is not changed here. Update the CI timing section of docs/git_flow.md: it currently says Stage 5 never reruns CI, which this change makes false for timing-gate-only failures on unchanged code; state the bounded rerun rule and that every job judged by the gate (unit on macOS and Ubuntu, and the Workspace survival job) uses it. Module line budgets (holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json) are frozen: never change that file; ci_final_head.py must stay within its existing line limit, and if it would exceed it, move the new helper code into a sibling module of the same package listed in scope instead of raising the limit.
rationale: Five timing-only failures in one day each withdrew a green approval and forced a full pipeline run and a full re-review, although the same code had passed minutes earlier. A bounded rerun on unchanged code separates runner noise from a real regression without weakening the gate, which still fails a head whose tests are slower or whose code changed.
acceptance_criteria: A test replays a timing-gate-only failure on a head whose changes are bookkeeping-only or empty: the first rerun fails and the second passes, the result is green and timing_rerun records two attempts.
A test shows that three failed reruns in a row return the failed record unchanged, with the attempt count recorded, so consensus is withdrawn only after the last attempt.
A test shows that a head with any changed code, test or workflow path is never rerun, and that a failure with a non-timing failing check or with pending checks is never rerun.

The record keys of the existing timing_rerun output keep their names and meanings; existing tests in test_final_head_timing_rerun.py and test_calibrate_final_head_ci.py still pass with at most the expectation changes the new attempt count requires.
docs/git_flow.md describes the bounded rerun and no longer says Stage 5 never reruns CI for timing-gate failures.
No file under .github/ and no workflow file is changed; scripts/ci_timing_gate.py is unchanged.
All tests pass via 'uv run pytest', and 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass.
